findings.title: On a paged note, a saved trailing space is hidden and the next letter lands before it
findings.scenario: On a new A4 note (default page preset, v2 contract), the draft ends in a space when the handoff happens. Paste 'hello ' into the empty draft (no race needed), or type 'hello ' and pause on a slow link. Then type x. Expected 'hello x'. Actual: the durable textarea shows 'hello' with the caret at 5, and the stored unit becomes 'hellox '. Two variants: 'one\ntwo ' then x gives units ['one','twox ']; a first line of '# ' then t gives '#t ', a literal with no heading. The handoff writes draftText.trimEnd() to blockTextDrafts while the flow keeps the space. noteBlocksToPageFlow (notePageFlowService.ts:28) sees flow text differ from text and rebuilds the measurement units from the trimmed text. paginateTextFlowSlices (paginationEditingService.ts:42) then clamps the slice end to 5, and PaginatedTextBlockProjection shows and replaces only that slice. This is the A18 symptom (a typed space ending up in the wrong place) in a new shape: the pre-change controller gives 'abcd', the post-change gives 'abcd '.
findings.evidence: RAN in wf3, jsdom, client/src/pages/Notes/canvasEngine/hooks/zzA18Trailing.test.tsx. Real parts: useDraftBlockController, useBlockDraftAuthority, noteBlocksToPageFlow, resolveDocumentPageFlowPlan (default estimator, not the DOM measurer), BlockEditorLayer, PaginatedTextBlockProjection, DraftBlockEditorLayer. createBlock and saveBlock are modelled on useNoteCanvasDataAdapter :1560-1620 and :1959-2190. Output: S2 ['abc '] plus d gives ['abcd ']; S5 gives ['one','twox ']; S7 gives ['#t ']; S11 paste 'hello ' plus x gives ['hellox ']. Same sequences with no fragments (TextBlockProjection, whose alignFlowWithText tolerates trimEnd) pass with ['abc d'], which is why the existing tests are green. Positive control: changing :619 to draftText made S2 and S5 pass and sent S7 through the heading request (text 't'); reverted, and the sha256 matches snapshot.txt. READ only: the same trim is at :460 (replay) and in the adapter at :1616, :1656, :2677, :2722. The restore paths (:2677, :2722) would hide a trailing space or blank line the same way after a block restore; that part predates this change.
findings.browser_check: New A4 note, double-click to start a draft, paste 'hello ' (with the trailing space), wait 2 seconds, type x, click away. Read the unit from GET /notes/:id/blocks. Expected 'hello x'; predicted 'hellox '.

findings.title: On a paged note, a draft ending in Enter never hands off and the draft box stays open
findings.scenario: On a new A4 note, the draft ends in a line break at handoff and nothing is typed after it. Paste 'copied line\n' (no race needed), or type 'abc', press Enter and stop while the first save is out. Expected: the box closes and the caret is on a new empty line in the block. Actual: the text half is trimmed to 'abc' at useDraftBlockController.ts:619, so the empty unit tu-2 gets no line in the page plan and no textarea. The new early return at BlockEditorLayer.tsx:413 then skips focus, and handleDurableFocusReceipt never runs. The draft box stays open beside the saved block, both showing 'abc'. Follow-ups: clicking elsewhere does not close it. Double-clicking elsewhere reopens the same box with 'abc\n' in it, and text typed there is saved as a second unit of the old block rather than a new block at the click. Selecting all, deleting and clicking away closes the box, but on the save path the server refuses the discard and 'abc' stays on the page. It does heal in two cases: typing on inside the box, or clicking into the block itself.
findings.evidence:
RAN in wf3, same harness. S1 'abc
' gives draftActive true, textDraft 'abc', flow ['abc',''], textareas 'abc' (tu-1) and draft 'abc
', draft focused. S3 paste and S4 two Enters behave the same. S8 after blur: draftActive still true. S10: activateDraft at a new layout (READ: this is what handlePageSpaceDoubleClick calls) shows value 'abc
'; after typing, flow is ['abc','new para']. S9 delete all then blur: draft closed, durable 'abc' remains, with discard mocked in that harness. Server half RAN separately: server/src/__tests__/zzA18Trailing.test.ts gets 409 'Client-created block has been meaningfully changed' for discard after a save. READ only: the adapter's error toast on that 409. Against the pre-change controller in the same harness, S1, S3 and S4 all close the box and focus the block, so the stuck box is a regression. Without fragments, S1 hands off correctly to tu-2. Positive control: untrimming :619 closes the box and focuses tu-2 in S1, S3, S4 and S8. Typing on heals because the text half then matches, which is why the K, W and H arms did not catch this.
findings.browser_check: New A4 note, double-click to start a draft, paste 'copied line' plus a newline, wait 2 seconds. Predicted: the draft box with its hint is still there and document.activeElement is the draft textarea. Click empty page space: the box stays. Reload: the unit list is ['copied line',''], so the stored data is fine.

findings.title: Escape cannot remove a slash trigger when the handed-off text is trimmed against the flow
findings.scenario:
In a draft, type 'abc', Enter, Enter, ArrowUp, then '/' on the middle line, and let the handoff happen with the slash menu open. Draft text is 'abc
/
'; the handoff publishes text 'abc
/' with flow ['abc','/','']. Press Escape. planSlashBlockRollback compares the flow join to the text, finds them different and rejects, so the '/' stays in the note.

findings.title: A draft discard is refused because an unrelated block has an annotation on the same unit id (predates this change)
findings.scenario: A person has an annotation on the first paragraph of any block, whose unit id is tu-1 as every paragraph's first unit is. In a new note they type 'a', delete it, and the discard fires. collectReferenceBlockers matches annotation_ranges by user and text_unit_id alone, so the unrelated annotation blocks the discard with a 409, and the block remains. The patch did not touch this query or its input ids, so this is not a regression. It is reported because it matches the 'empty block that cannot be discarded' category.
findings.evidence: RAN in wf3 server, real routes on an in-memory DB: server/src/__tests__/zzA18Trailing.test.ts. Annotation on tu-1 of another block, then create with key k9 and discard: 409 {'error':'Client-created block has durable references','details':{'blockers':['annotation']}}, with 2 blocks left. READ only: the client path through discardDraftBlock to its toast.
findings.browser_check: With an annotation already on any first paragraph, open a new note, type a, immediately delete it before the first save returns, click away, and look for 'Empty draft cleanup could not be confirmed' with the block still present.

findings.title: A word typed after a trailing space goes in front of that space on a paged block
findings.scenario: New note, first block on a page. Type `hello`, then a space while the create is still out. Stop until the block takes over, then type `world`. Expected `hello world`. Got `helloworld ` in the DOM and the flow. The space is kept in the flow but hidden: line 619 publishes `draftText.trimEnd()` beside the untrimmed flow, so `noteBlocksToPageFlow` sees the two differ and rebuilds units from the trimmed text. The page plan then ends at offset 5, the textarea shows `hello`, and `replaceSliceText` puts each key before the hidden space. Line 460 has the same trim. The Result note says trailing spaces are now handled; that holds only on the unpaginated surface.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness (real controllers, real BlockEditorLayer, real useNotePageFlow, jsdom, gated network). Paged: after handover the textarea is `hello` at caret 5 and the flow is [`hello `]; after typing, the text is `helloworld `. Flat surface: `hello world`. Pre-change paged: `helloworld`, so this is not fixed, only moved. Positive control: dropping the trim at lines 619 and 460 gives `hello world` on the paged surface. Read only: a real first block is paged, because the default contract is v2 (db/init.ts) and the default draft layout has no width_mode, so isFlowBlock accepts it. Also read only: restoreBlockById publishes the same trimmed text, so undo then redo should bring the mismatch back.
findings.browser_check: With the matrix proxy at 200ms: new note, Input.insertText `hello`, wait 30ms, press space, wait 1500ms, type `world`. Read the textarea values and the server units; expect `hello world`.

findings.title: Enter then stop on a paged block: the handover never completes and the draft stays open
findings.scenario: New note. Type `First`, press Enter while the create is out, then stop typing. Expected: the draft closes and the caret sits on an empty second line of the block. Got: focus stays in the draft, `draftActive` stays true, and the durable block is mounted alongside it showing only `First`. The receipt names tu-2, but tu-2 never gets a textarea because the trimmed text at useDraftBlockController.ts:619 removes the empty unit from the page plan (notePageFlowService.ts:28-29). The effect does re-run on every surface render, because autoFocusSelection is a new object each time, but it returns at line 413 every time. Nothing changes until the person's next key, which goes to the draft and triggers a new save and handover. The matrix stays green because it only inspects state after that next key.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness on the paged surface. After the save returned and 10 scheduler turns: active=draft-1, textareas=[block-1/tu-1 `First`, draft-1 `First\n`], server=[First, ''], draftActive=true. Flat surface: active=block-1/tu-2, draft gone. Pre-change paged: moved to the block at caret 0, so the next key gave `SFirst`. The early return swaps that bug for this one. Positive control without the trim: active=block-1/tu-2 at 0, draft closed. Read only: .draftBlock has a transparent background and the draft layout starts where the block sits, so the two probably overlap visually. Not seen in a browser.
findings.browser_check: insertText `First`, wait 30ms, press Enter, wait 2000ms, press nothing further. Evaluate document.activeElement.closest('[data-draft-editor]') and count [data-draft-editor]. Both should be empty; look at the page for doubled text.

findings.title: flushSync does not reach setBlocks, so a key after an uninterrupted create still lands in the draft and is misplaced
findings.scenario: New note. The first input arrives as one event (IME commit or paste of `abc`) and nothing else is typed during the create. When the create returns, flushSync commits without the block, because createDraftBlock's setBlocks is default priority. Focus stays in the draft until React's next scheduler task, so the comment at line 578 is false on this path. Press Enter in that gap, then X. Expected lines `abc` and `X`. Got `abcX` and an empty line, because the receipt is still tu-1 and the block's focus effect returns early once focus is inside. A character in the gap on a paged block also resets the caret, because PaginatedTextBlockProjection replays the selection it captured on focus, before setSelectionRange ran. `abc`, then `d`, then `e` gave `eabcd` in jsdom.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness with a commit trace: `render blocks=0 recon=true focus=block-1 draftActive=true`, then active=draft-1 after 40 further microtasks, then `render blocks=1` only after a macrotask. Enter case on both surfaces: [`abcX`, '']. Character case, paged: `eabcd`; flat: `abcde`. Pre-change: paged character case identical; the Enter case also gave `abcX`. jsdom hides this by default: it leaves window.event stuck on `focusin`, which made setBlocks synchronous until I stubbed window.event to undefined, which is what a browser's promise continuation sees (read only: an XHR `loadend` event is also default priority). A browser may start the caret at the end of the text rather than 0, which would give `abced`; not run. Gap width in a real browser not measured.
findings.browser_check: Hold the placement PUT in the proxy, insertText `abc`, release the hold, and send Enter then X by CDP as soon as the response arrives. Repeat 30 times, with CPU throttle 6x. Failing samples read `abcX` plus an empty line.

findings.title: The handover's republish ignores replay mode and wipes what was typed into the durable editor
findings.scenario: `abc`, create returns, `d` lands in the draft in the gap, that save fails, focus is now in the block. Click away and back: handleDurableFocusReceipt starts a replay whose save carries preserveDrafts:true, precisely so the authority is left alone. Type K while it is out. When it returns, lines 618-621 publish the response flow unconditionally, without checking replayingHandoffRef, and K disappears from the screen. Regression from this change.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness. Post-change, paged: `Kabcd` before the response, `abcd` after; flat: `abcdK` then `abcd`. Same steps on the pre-change sources: `Kabcd` and `abcdK` survive on the same surfaces. The server log shows the replay's save flagged preserve. The real useTextFlowHistory was not mounted; read only: its open session still holds K, so a later seal could write K to the server while the DOM lacks it, or further typing could drop it for good.
findings.browser_check: Hard to time by hand. Use the proxy: fail one PUT right after the block takes over, click out and back, type K with the next PUT held, release, compare the textarea with the server.

findings.title: Typing in the durable editor during a save started by a gap key is wiped when that save returns
findings.scenario: `abc`, create returns, `d` lands in the draft in the gap and starts a save with preserveDrafts false; the flag is read before the durable focus sets it (line 565). The durable editor takes focus and the person keeps typing `YZ` during the round trip. When the save returns, the text goes back to `abcd` and YZ is gone. The next key lands at the old caret (`Q` gave `abcdQ` flat, `abQcd` paged). Pressing Enter in the gap and then typing behaves the same: `X` vanishes and the screen and server end at [`abc`, ''].
findings.evidence: Ran the harness. Flat: `abcdYZ`, then `abcd` when the save returned. Paged: `YZabcd`, then `abcd`. Identical on the pre-change sources, so not a regression, but this change does not address it and adds a second overwrite at line 619. The harness copies the adapter's publish rather than running the adapter. Read only: the open edit session still holds the typed text, so without further typing the server can keep text the DOM has lost.
findings.browser_check: Proxy at 400ms: insertText `abc`, send `d` as the create returns, then type `YZ` before the next PUT returns. Compare the DOM and the server after everything settles.

findings.title: After a failed replay, clicking back into the block overwrites durable text with stale draft text, on the server too
findings.scenario: `abc`, create returns, `d` in the gap, that save fails. The draft stays alive behind the block with pendingReconciliationRef still set. Type Y in the block and click away; the blur save succeeds, so the server holds `Yabcd`. Click back into the block: the revision mismatch at line 455 adopts the old draft text into the authority and saves it. Screen and server both become `abcd`. Y is lost after it was already saved.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness on both surfaces. Server log: save [`abcd`], save [`Yabcd`], save [`abcd`] flagged preserve. Final DOM and server `abcd`. Identical on the pre-change sources, so not a regression. Read only: the real textHistory.saveBlock path has no branch that stops this overwrite. It sends the draft text unless it matches the last save or a failed transaction exists.
findings.browser_check: Proxy: fail one PUT right after handover, type Y in the block, click the title, let the blur save pass, click back in the block, reload, and read the text.

findings.title: After pasting a paragraph that spans two pages, the next key lands in the middle of it
findings.scenario: New note. Paste one long paragraph (8103 characters here) that spills onto a second page. After handover, type X. Expected at the end of the paste. Got X at offset 4959, at the end of page one. `textareas.find` takes the first slice of the unit, and the logical offset is clamped to that slice's length. The projection's own pageSliceForCaret is not used here.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness with the estimator line measurer, because jsdom has no layout to measure: two slices of lengths 4959 and 3144, focus on the first at 4959, `X` at index 4959 of 8104, surrounded by `ipsum dolor Xsit amet lo`. Identical on the pre-change sources, so not a regression, but the same line was edited for this goal.
findings.browser_check: Paste a two-page single paragraph into a new note's first block, wait for handover, press X, and find it in the text.

findings.title: The handover moves focus while an IME composition is open
findings.scenario: New note with a Chinese IME. Type `ni` and pause on the candidate list for longer than one round trip. The save loop ends and focus moves to the durable editor mid-composition. Nothing in the draft path or the focus effect checks composition, and the raw pinyin has already gone to the server. Expected: the chosen characters. Likely result: raw letters committed or the composition cancelled, and the candidate key landing in the durable editor as plain input.
findings.evidence: Ran in jsdom: fired compositionstart, then input `n` and `i`, released create and save. Focus moved to block-1 with no compositionend, and the server holds `ni`. Identical on the pre-change sources. grep found no composition handling in DraftBlockEditorLayer, useDraftBlockController or useRuntimeNaturalWritingController. What the browser does with the open composition is inferred, not run; the handoff also lists real IME as unverified.
findings.browser_check: Real IME, proxy at 400ms: new note, type `nihao` and hold on the candidate window for 2 seconds, then pick a candidate. Read the text and the server.

findings.title: A caret moved off the `# ` line before handover is pulled onto the heading
findings.scenario: During the first create, type `abc`, Enter, `# T`, then press Up so the caret is in `abc`. Handover correctly focuses tu-1. One frame later the new effect sends a heading request whose focus is always the heading unit, so the caret jumps to the heading and the next key meant for `abc` lands there. This is narrow: it needs a caret move inside the first-save window. In the durable editor the caret is always on the line being converted, so this is new with the draft path.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness with a spy on onHeadingStructure: active=block-1/tu-1 at 1, request focus=tu-2@1. Read only, not run: useHeadingStructureController.ts applies that focus with editor.focus() and setSelectionRange, and replays queued keys at it.
findings.browser_check: Proxy at 400ms: insertText `abc`, Enter, insertText `# T`, press ArrowUp, wait for handover, type Q, and see which line holds Q.

findings.title: A leftover receipt blocks later requests to focus the block
findings.scenario: New note: `a`, Enter, `b` during the create, so the receipt is tu-2. In the block, Backspace at the start of `b` merges the lines, so tu-2 no longer exists. Click away. Something then asks for block focus (panel entry, pending link). focusBlockId is set but nothing focuses, because the reconciliation lives until the next draft and line 413 returns. Keys go nowhere until the person clicks into the text. Pre-change this fell back to the first textarea.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness on both surfaces. Post-change after setFocusBlockId: no active editor, focus=block-1. Same steps on the pre-change sources: active=block-1/tu-1, focus cleared. Regression. Which UI entries reach this was read, not clicked.

findings.title: Enter then a key records block creation twice in undo history
findings.scenario: Paged block: `First`, Enter, stop, then type `S`. The first run records createdBlock. The second run's flushSync now moves focus, handleDurableFocusReceipt runs clearLocalDraft inside it, durableHistoryRecordedRef resets, and line 626 records createdBlock again. After undoing the block, one more Ctrl+Z does nothing visible, and redo has a matching dead press.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness: history=[created:block-1, created:block-1]. Pre-change and with the trim removed: one entry. The harness counts entries and does not run the real undo stack. Read only: the second undo calls DELETE on a trashed block, and routes/noteBlocks.ts returns 200, so the entry moves to redo with no effect.
findings.browser_check: insertText `First`, Enter, wait 2 seconds, type S, then press Ctrl+Z until the block goes and once more. The extra press should do nothing.

findings.title: A pasted `# ` last line stays literal when no key was typed during the create
findings.scenario: Paste `abc\n# T` as the first input and wait. The new effect runs during the flushSync commit, when `blocks` does not yet hold the block. `before` is undefined, it returns, and its only dependency is the reconciliation, so it never runs again. The text stays `# T`. The same text typed with a save loop becomes a heading.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness on both surfaces with a spy on onHeadingStructure. Paste: no request, flow [`abc`, `# T`]. Typed: one request, [paragraph abc, heading_1 T].
findings.browser_check: Paste `abc` plus a newline plus `# T` into a new note and wait 2 seconds. Compare with the same text typed during the create.

findings.title: `# Title` on the first line becomes a heading or stays literal depending on network timing
findings.scenario: Type `#`, space, `T` on the first line of a new note. If handover happens after `#`, the space reaches the durable editor and the line becomes a heading. If all three keys land during the first save, `live.length < 2` refuses the request and `# T` stays literal for good. The same keys give different documents depending on round-trip time.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness. Keys during create: no request, flow [`# T`] as paragraph. Handover after `#`: flow heading_1 `T`. Pre-change also lacked any draft heading request; the new rule does not cover this case.
findings.browser_check: Type `# T` at 25ms spacing with the proxy at 400ms, and again at the same spacing with no added latency. Compare the writing role on the server.

findings.title: A note switch during the first save flattens paragraphs into one unit
findings.scenario: Type `a`, Enter, `b` while the create is out, then switch notes. resetDraft reads draftTextFlowRef, which is null on this path, so the recovery receipt has no contentJson. The finalizer falls back to contentForTemplate, which makes one unit holding `a\nb`. On return the two paragraphs are one unit with a line break inside, unlike every other save path.
findings.evidence: Ran the harness: the stored receipt has text `a\nb` and no content, and contentForTemplate gives units [`a\nb`]. The finalizer itself was stubbed, so that step is read, not run. The same one-unit shape rendered both lines in one textarea in the harness, so no text is hidden; only the structure is wrong. Not touched by this change.

reviews.coverage:
Harness: real useRuntimeNaturalWritingController (with useDraftBlockController and useSlashCommandController), useBlockDraftAuthority, useBlockSelectionController, useNotePageFlow, BlockEditorLayer with both text projections, and DraftWritingEntryLayer, in jsdom with real React scheduling and no act(). The network is gated. createDraftBlock's and saveBlock's publishes are copied at the same priority, not the real adapter. Keys are native input events dispatched at document.activeElement. window.event is stubbed to undefined (jsdom leaves it on `focusin`, which hides the gap). The scenarios were also run on the pre-change sources by swapping the four files in wf1 and restoring them; cmp confirms they match the post tree. Harness files are in <tmp>\r04a\wf1\client\src\pages\Notes\canvasEngine\hooks: a18harness.tsx and a18review.test.tsx through a18review4.test.tsx.

Not run: any browser, real server, real IME, real useTextFlowHistory, real undo stack, real useHeadingStructureController commit, or the existing client suite. Anything depending on those is marked read only in its finding. That a real first block is paged is from reading the code, not an end-to-end run.

Probed, no defect found:
- Memo keyed only by text: draftTextFlowFromText is deterministic (same ids for the same text), the only in-place unit write found by grep is on a private extracted copy, and two drafts with the same text in one note and across a note switch did not interfere.
- flushSync: no React flushSync error was captured in the second scenario batch (a18review2), which includes persistDraft running from a blur during a commit; the first batch had no such capture. The await keeps it out of commits.
- Keys between the last loop check and the flush: only microtasks run there, so no key can land. The real gap is after the flush, in the third finding.
- Note switch during a create: the run stops at requestIsCurrent and does not flush.
- Ctrl+Z while the draft has focus: the keyboard handler ignores unmanaged textareas (read only), so undo in the stuck-draft state stays native.
- Early-return re-runs: the effect does re-run on each surface render because autoFocusSelection is a fresh object; the problem is the unit never arriving.

findings.title: A caret on another line is thrown to the end of the heading, and the person's keys follow it
findings.scenario: In a new note, type `Intro`, Enter, `# Title` before the save returns. Then go back to line 1 with Up or a click, and keep writing after a pause of one round trip. Handoff puts the caret correctly on line 1, but the frame sends a heading request with focus at the end of the heading, because the caret is not on that unit. Typing ` more` for line 1 during the commit gives `Intro` / `Title more`, where `Intro more` / `Title` was intended. With no keys at all, the caret still jumps from line 1 to the end of the heading. A variant: select `Title` in the draft to retype it and type `New` during the commit, and the result is `NewTitle`. The commit keeps only selectionStart, so the selection is not replaced.

Line 619 publishes the trimmed text beside the untrimmed flow, so the page plan ends at offset 5 and the space cannot be reached in that textarea. With the pre-change sources in the same full runtime the result is `helloworld`. So "not fixed, only moved" holds: the joined words are not new, and the space went from lost to misplaced.

**Flat surface**
A Web long page note gives `hello world`, also confirmed.

- Read only: new notes default to `a4_portrait`.
